title: Finite sampled observations versus the asymptotic diffusion class
status: Exploratory deterministic calculation specified after preliminary covariance and KL calculations. Not a preregistered discovery test or a new fitted-model benchmark.
units: Mass, thermal energy, and fractional friction scale equal one; all times, frequencies, and diffusion coefficients are dimensionless.
family: gamma_epsilon(t) = exp(-epsilon*t)/sqrt(pi*t); Ctilde_epsilon(s) = 1/(s + (s+epsilon)^(-1/2)), principal square root
observation_model: M independent, exactly sampled, stationary zero-mean Gaussian velocity vectors; each vector has 20 entries at times 0, 0.6, ..., 11.4. No sensor error, nuisance parameters, forcing, or reconstruction compression is included.
bound: For any test with size at most alpha at epsilon=0, power at epsilon>0 is at most min(1, alpha + sqrt(M*KL(N(0,K_epsilon)||N(0,K_0))/2)). This is a rigorous statistical inequality evaluated in floating-point arithmetic, not an achieved detector power or interval-certified numerical bound.
covariance_method: Analytic inverse Laplace transform using the three roots of z^3-epsilon*z+1, partial fractions, and scaled complementary error functions; checked against independent zero-cutoff quadrature and the Volterra equation.
kl_method: Cholesky-whitened covariance difference and eigenvalues; use a small-argument series for a-log1p(a); independently compare with direct trace/log-determinant and generalized-eigenvalue formulas.
scope_limits: No finite-data result for ideal continuous-path observation or exact correlation oracles is claimed.
Gaussian equilibrium preparation and independent repetitions are assumptions. FDT alone does not imply Gaussian statistics.
The asymptotic exponent is discontinuous at zero cutoff; D_epsilon=sqrt(epsilon) itself is continuous.
A large upper bound is inconclusive; a small bound constrains every test under the stated experiment.
These cutoffs are development examples. The physical tempered-memory family has established prior art.
